tagline: Leading U.S. homebuilder and mortgage banking services provider
hero_kpi_rationale: Gross margin is the key KPI in the residential homebuilding sector. It reflects NVR's ability to maintain profitability amid pricing pressures and rising construction costs.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue that remains after paying direct construction costs.
kpis.description: Homebuilding gross margin declined from 23.7% in 2024 to 21.2% in 2025, impacted by a weak demand environment and community-level adjustments.
kpis.signal: Margin under pressure in 2025 due to price adjustments in a tight market.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned from home sales and mortgage services.
kpis.description: Total homebuilding revenue decreased from $10,292.425M in 2024 to $10,094.269M in 2025, down 2%, primarily due to a 4% drop in homes settled.
kpis.signal: Slight decline in 2025 despite stable pricing, driven by fewer homes sold.

kpis.name: Home Settlements (units)
kpis.explanation: Number of homes completed and sold during the year.
kpis.description: Settlements declined 4% in 2025 (21,915 units) following growth in 2024 (22,836 units), reflecting slowing demand.
kpis.signal: Fourth consecutive year of growth followed by a decline in 2025.

kpis.name: New Orders (units)
kpis.explanation: Number of new homes ordered by buyers.
kpis.description: New orders fell 10% in 2025 (20,410 units) versus 22,560 in 2024, indicating weakening demand.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in 2025, signaling low buyer confidence.

kpis.name: Backlog Units
kpis.explanation: Number of homes sold but not yet delivered.
kpis.description: Unit backlog declined 15% (8,448 units in 2025 versus 9,953 in 2024), reflecting the drop in new orders.
kpis.signal: Backlog sharply lower, a warning signal for future revenues.

kpis.name: Backlog Value
kpis.explanation: Total value of homes sold but not yet delivered.
kpis.description: Backlog value decreased from $4,791.870M in 2024 to $4,008.043M in 2025, down 16%, driven by fewer orders and lower average selling prices.
kpis.signal: Backlog declining in value and volume, pressure on 2026 revenues.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Final profit after all costs and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income fell 20% in 2025 to $1,339.816M, hurt by lower margins and volumes.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in net income in 2025, more pronounced than revenue.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue sourced from SEC EDGAR company facts XBRL over the last eight reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Total revenue of $10.324B in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.signal: Margin under pressure in 2025 due to price adjustments in a tight market.

risks.title: High interest rates affecting demand
risks.score_rationale: The risk is repeatedly mentioned in the 10-K, with strong language ("material adverse effect"). It is central to profitability and demand, and its severity is amplified by dependence on credit affordability. The Macro category is highly weighted.

risks.title: Limited access to mortgage financing
risks.score_rationale: The text emphasizes that nearly all customers depend on mortgage credit. A tightening of credit conditions is presented as potentially having a direct "material adverse effect" on sales and cash flows. The language is urgent and repeated.

risks.title: Residential inventory impairment
risks.score_rationale: The risk is well documented with mention of potential losses through forfeited deposits and impairments. The language is concerned but less alarming than macro risks. It is a key structural risk in the real estate sector.

risks.title: Increased competition in homebuilding and mortgage lending
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly mentioned for both core businesses (homebuilding and lending). The language indicates pressure on pricing, quality, and incentives, impacting profitability. Less existential than macro risks.

risks.title: Cyberattacks and data breaches
risks.score_rationale: The text describes active security measures but acknowledges persistent vulnerabilities. Mentions severe legal, financial, and reputational consequences. The risk is rising with AI, but still moderate compared to economic risks.

risks.title: Shortage of materials or labor
risks.score_rationale: The risk is clearly identified with reference to delays and increased costs. The language is concerned but not alarmist. It fits within the context of margin pressure, but not an existential threat.

risks.title: Mortgage loan repurchase obligations
risks.score_rationale: The text warns of significant losses if loans sold into the secondary market fail to meet representations and warranties. The risk involves penalties, repurchases, or indemnifications, with strong language ("material adverse effect"). Highly specific to the mortgage lending business.

ai_positioning.summary: NVR does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
